summary: post_reel.py's shared try/finally unconditionally fires on EVERY early return from inside the try block (Python semantics), including the verify-only (:121) and DRY-ok (:181) returns -- which behavioral-spec.md's own Ground Truth section explicitly says are 'NOT failure paths... out of scope for the outcome vocabulary.' The finally's res.setdefault("outcome","failed") therefore injects an unwanted outcome:"failed" key into both of those JSON shapes, AND causes every one of the 9 early-return paths (not-logged-in, account-guard, before-unstable-abort, no-create-btn, file-chooser-fail, video-never-loaded, no-share-btn, verify-only, DRY-ok) to print the JSON dict TWICE to stdout instead of once.
description:
post_reel.py:90 opens a `try:` block that runs through the rest of main(). Every one of the 9 early-return sites inside it (lines 97, 111, 121, 134, 139/146/153/175 for the 6 pre-share failure sites, and 181 for DRY-ok) does `print(json.dumps(res, ...)); return`. Because Python executes a matching `finally:` clause on EVERY exit from its try block -- including an explicit `return` -- the shared finally at lines 210-212 (`res.setdefault("outcome", "failed"); print(json.dumps(res, ensure_ascii=False))`) ALSO fires after each of these returns, before the function actually returns. This was empirically verified with a minimal repro (`def f(): 
  try: print('A'); return
  finally: print('B')` -> prints 'A' then 'B'), then traced against the real file's exact line numbers. Concretely: (1) the verify-only return at :121 prints `{...,"reels":[...],"ok":true,...}` WITHOUT an outcome key, then the finally re-prints the SAME dict WITH an added `"outcome":"failed"` key -- contradicting behavioral-spec.md line 40 ('verify-only-mode return and :169 DRY-ok are NOT failure paths... out of scope for the outcome vocabulary'). (2) The DRY-ok return at :181 has the identical problem. (3) All 9 early-return paths print their JSON dict TWICE, contradicting the Ground Truth section's own stated contract: 'post_reel.py returns ONE json dict via print(json.dumps(res, ...))' (behavioral-spec.md line 24). This is also a direct, traceable violation of PROP-004(c)(iii)'s explicit test assertion (verification-architecture.md, proof-obligations table): 'the run reaches "reached":"DRY-ok" exactly as it does today, with no added `outcome` field beyond what dry mode already emits' -- a faithful implementation of that literal test would FAIL against the current code, since the last (and only observably-distinct) printed line for a dry run DOES carry an added outcome field.
productionImpact: Currently LOW for the two real consumers: run.sh takes `| tail -1` of the subprocess's stdout (only the finally's re-print survives, and for the 6 true pre-share failure sites the added outcome value is identical to what the path already set, so run.sh's 3-way routing is unaffected). self_heal.py's `_call_verify_only` also reads only `out.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1]` and only consumes `.get("ok")`/`.get("reels")`, neither of which the extra `outcome` key touches. Neither run.sh (always passes --live) nor self_heal.py ever exercises dry mode. So no current production path is functionally broken by this -- but it is a genuine, concrete deviation from the approved spec's own explicit scoping statement and its own required test assertion, and it silently corrupts the documented JSON shape for two 'successful mode' paths (verify-only, DRY-ok) that a future consumer (or a human debugging manually) would reasonably expect to match the Ground Truth's documented shape.
